en: The Hayagrīva Upaniṣad
May that Lord Hayāsya, by whose grace even one who knows little may attain knowledge and its fruit,
shine forever within my heart.
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O worshipful ones. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise you.
May we attain that lifespan ordained by the gods.
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being;
may Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being;
may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are uninjured, grant us well-being.
May Bṛhaspati grant us well-being.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.

Hari, Om! Nārada, having approached Brahmā, said: "Teach me, O Blessed One, the most excellent knowledge of Brahman (brahmavidyā), by which, having quickly cast off all evil and attained the knowledge of Brahman, one becomes possessed of sovereignty."
Brahmā said:
He who knows the mantras having Hayagrīva as their presiding deity knows the Śruti, Smṛti, Itihāsa, and Purāṇas;
he becomes possessed of all sovereign powers.
These are the mantras:
Salutation to You, O Hayagrīva, the King of Vidyās, whose nature transcends all, and who consists of consciousness and bliss; svāhā, svāhā, salutation! (1)

Salutation, Svāhā, Svāhā, salutation to the one whose form consists of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas; to the one whose deed was the retrieval of the Vedas; to the one whose body is the Praṇava and the Udgītha; to the Great Horse-Headed One (Mahāśvaśiras). || 2 ||
O Udgītha, O Praṇava-Udgītha, Lord of all masters of speech, inconceivable one consisting of all the Vedas, awaken me, awaken me; Svāhā, Svāhā! Salutations! || 3 ||
The sages are Brahmā, Atri, Arka, Savitṛ, and Bhārgava;
the meters are Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, and Anuṣṭubh;
the deity is the glorious Hayagrīva, the Supreme Self.
*Lhauṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*). *So'ham* is the power (*śakti*).
*Lhūṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*).
The application for worldly enjoyment and liberation;
the ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*) by means of the syllables *a*, *u*, and *m*;
and meditation.
We worship Hayagrīva, who has four arms, is enriched with the conch, the discus, the great mudrā, and the book,
and resembles the full moon.
"Oṃ śrīmiti" consists of two syllables;
"lhaum" consists of one syllable;
and "oṃ namo bhagavate" consists of seven syllables.
"Hayagrīvāya" consists of five syllables;
"viṣṇave" consists of three syllables;
and "mahyam medhām prajñām" [consists of eight syllables].
The six syllables are "prayaccha," and the five syllables are "svāhā";
this constitutes the fourth part of Hayagrīva. || 4 ||
*Oṃ śrīmiti* consists of two syllables;
*lhaum* consists of one syllable;
and *aim aim aim* consists of three syllables.
*Klīṃ klīṃ*—these are two syllables. *Sauḥ sauḥ*—these are two syllables. *Hrīṃ*—this is one syllable.
"Oṃ namo bhagavate" consists of seven syllables.
"Mahyaṃ medhāṃ prajñām" consists of six syllables.
"Prayaccha svāhā" consists of five syllables.
The fifth Manu comes into being. || 5 ||
I shall proclaim the Brahma-vidyā by means of the single-syllable Hayagrīva mantra.
Brahmā [taught it] to Maheśvara; Maheśvara to Saṃkarṣaṇa; Saṃkarṣaṇa to Nārada;
Nārada to Vyāsa; and Vyāsa bestowed it upon the worlds.
The triad consisting of the syllables *ha*, *kāra*, and *ma* becomes a single form.
*Lhauṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bījākṣara*).
Through the seed-syllable in the form of *lhauṃ*, both prosperity and eloquence (*sārasvatī*) accrue to those who recite it.
For those who know its true nature, liberation from the body (vaidehī-mukti) occurs;
one becomes the sovereign of the guardians of the quarters, kings, nāgas, and kinnaras.
By the power of the practice of reciting the single-syllable Hayagrīva mantra, the sun and other celestial bodies proceed spontaneously in their respective functions.
Among all seed-syllables (*bīja*), the single-syllable seed-mantra of Hayagrīva is supreme; it is the essence of the king of mantras.
By [reciting] *lhauṃ*, one becomes the very embodiment of Hayagrīva.
Amṛtaṃ kurukuru svāhā! For those who recite this, there arises perfection of speech, the attainment of prosperity, and the accomplishment of the eightfold yoga.
One becomes purified from the act of approaching those who should not be approached.
By conversing with those who have fallen [from their status], one becomes purified;
one is liberated from sins such as the killing of a Brahmin.
Like a householder entering his home, the embodied soul enters the Supreme Self at the end of the body.
These mantras establish the meaning taught by the great sayings (*mahāvākya*): "Brahman is consciousness and bliss," "That thou art," "This self is Brahman," and "I am Brahman."
These are twofold, distinguished by vowels and consonants.
Then he mutters the following consecratory formulas (*anumantraṇa*):
"Whatever the voice utters, though it be unconscious—the delightful queen of the gods has sat down."
She milked out four [cows] for strength and nourishment; where indeed has her highest part gone? || 1 ||
Gaurī has lowed, fashioning the waters; she is one-footed, two-footed, four-footed;
she has become eight-footed, nine-footed, possessing a thousand syllables in the highest heaven. 2.
The nakulī with lips as its cover, surrounded by teeth as its rim, is the mistress of all speech; "Make me speak here beautifully"—this is the essence of speech. 3.
Driving away the mind of the serpent-like one, the great [hymn] bestowed by Jamadagni has roared aloud;
it has spread abroad the sun’s rays, glory, immortality, and agelessness among the gods. 4.
Whoever recites this knowledge of Brahman on the eleventh lunar day becomes a great person through the power of Hayagrīva;
he becomes liberated while living.
Om, salutations to Brahman! May there be retention for me, may there be no forgetting; may I be a retainer [of this knowledge] in my ears.
This has been heard by me from the east; "Om," this is the Upaniṣad concerning me.
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods;
may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O worshipful ones. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise you and attain that lifespan ordained by the gods.
Oṃ! May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being;
may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being;
may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unharmed, grant us well-being.
May Bṛhaspati grant us well-being.
Om, peace, peace, peace! Hariḥ Om, that is the Truth.
Thus ends the Hayagrīva Upaniṣad.
